title: Batch Two Crunches Loudly  (第二批咔嚓作响)

segments.t: 五分钟后，欧文得意洋洋地把二号烤模放在木质晾凉板上，而他的弟弟凯勒布循着香甜的焦糖气息走进咖啡角落，站到了泰莎身边。请先听一遍对话。
Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!
It smells like a street festival, Owen, though the top looks surprisingly shiny.
How many spoons of coarse sugar did you sprinkle under the hot grill, Owen?
Enough to give every slice a satisfying crisp snap when your fork goes down!
Let me press my dessert fork gently right in the middle... tap, tap, clang!
Oh dear — a cake is not supposed to ring like the front desk bell, Owen!
Speaking professionally as an architect, we could roof the bicycle shed with Batch Two.
Hey! Break through the top crust and taste the warm almond cake underneath!
Oh, underneath that sugar helmet, the berries and ground almonds are delicious!
So lemon alone is too sour, and dry sugar alone turns into courtyard stone.
What soft, shining glaze could possibly be hiding beneath that blue ink smudge, Tessa?
Bring me that green botanical book again — our noses might read better than our eyes!
下面我们逐句来看这第二批号称“酥脆”的蛋糕。
Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!
“快过来看看，小老弟！闻闻二号烤模上那层烤焦糖脆皮！”欧文像集市摊主吆喝一样热情；Step right up 相当于“大家快来看、请上前一步”：
Step right up, little brother!
英语没有中文“小……”或者“-儿”这样的单一后缀，通常在名词前加 little 来表示亲昵或年幼，比如 little brother。
toasted brown sugar crust
brown sugar 是红糖（黄糖），前面所有的修饰语全都叠放在中心词 crust（脆皮）之前。
It smells like a street festival, Owen, though the top looks surprisingly shiny.
“闻起来像街头集市一样香，欧文，不过表面看起来亮得有点出奇。”用 smell（闻起来）接名词时，英语必须加上介词 like（smell like）：
It smells like a street festival,
如果不加 like，smell 后面就直接跟形容词，比如 it smells good。
though the top looks surprisingly shiny.
though（不过、虽然）读作 /ðoʊ/，其中的 gh 不发音；look 加上形容词表示“看起来怎么样”。
How many spoons of coarse sugar did you sprinkle under the hot grill, Owen?
“欧文，你在炙烤的烤箱顶火下撒了多少勺粗砂糖？”泰莎追问具体用量；对 spoons 这类可数名词提问用 how many，不可数名词才用 how much：
How many spoons of coarse sugar
coarse（粗糙的、粗粒的）是 fine（细的）的反义词，它的读音和 course 完全一样。
did you sprinkle under the hot grill,
sprinkle 是“撒”，而 grill 在这里指的是烤箱上层的炙烤火。
Enough to give every slice a satisfying crisp snap when your fork goes down!
“足够让每一块在叉子切下去的时候，都发出惬意又清脆的‘咔嚓’声！”口语中直接用 Enough（足够了）来回答，非常自然地道。
a satisfying crisp snap
snap 指物体崩断或咬断时的脆响，crisp 形容像刚烤好的饼干那样爽脆。注意这三个词在英文里的排列顺序和中文刚好相反。
Let me press my dessert fork gently right in the middle... tap, tap, clang!
“让我把甜点叉轻轻往正中间一按……嗒，嗒，当啷！”凯勒布用 Let me + 动词原形礼貌而随意地请求试一下：
Let me press my dessert fork gently
副词 gently（轻轻地）放在宾语后面，不能插在动词 press 和宾语 my fork 之间。
right in the middle...
放在介词前面时，right 不是“右边”，而是“恰好、正好”。
Oh dear — a cake is not supposed to ring like the front desk bell, Owen!
“天哪——欧文，蛋糕可不该像前台呼叫铃那样叮当响啊！”Oh dear 是一句温和、略带老派礼貌的惊叹，表示担心或吃惊。
a cake is not supposed to ring
be supposed to 用来表达按常理“应该、理应”发生的事。连读时，d 常和 to 融在一起，读作 /səˈpoʊstə/。
Speaking professionally as an architect, we could roof the bicycle shed with Batch Two.
“作为一名专业建筑师来说，用第二批蛋糕都能给自行车棚铺屋顶了。”凯勒布一本正经地打趣道：
Speaking professionally as an architect,
表示某人的职业身份时，英语通常要加不定冠词，例如 as an architect、I am a nurse。
we could roof the bicycle shed
这里的 roof 用作动词，意思是“给……铺屋顶”；shed 指花园或院子里的小棚屋。
Hey! Break through the top crust and taste the warm almond cake underneath!
“喂！敲开上面的脆皮，尝尝底下温热的杏仁蛋糕啊！”欧文连用两个祈使句为自己的作品辩护：
Break through the top crust
短语动词 break through 意思是“击破、穿透”。
taste the warm almond cake underneath!
taste 是“品尝”；underneath（在底下）可以独自放在句末，后面不用再接名词。
Oh, underneath that sugar helmet, the berries and ground almonds are delicious!
“哦，在那层糖壳‘头盔’底下，浆果和杏仁粉还真美味！”尝了里面的蛋糕后，凯勒布立刻改口称赞：
that sugar helmet,
helmet（头盔）是个风趣的比喻；词首的 h 要轻声送气。
ground almonds
这里的 ground 是 grind（研磨）的过去分词（grind, ground, ground），意思是“磨碎的”，和表示“地面”的 ground 碰巧同形。
So lemon alone is too sour, and dry sugar alone turns into courtyard stone.
“这么说来，单用柠檬太酸，单用干糖又会变成庭院铺路石。”泰莎总结出规律，句首的 So 相当于“那么、所以”：
lemon alone is too sour,
放在名词后面的 alone 意思是“单独、仅仅”；sour 是“酸的”，too 表示“过于、太”。
turns into courtyard stone.
turn into 用来表示形态转变，意思是“变成……”。
What soft, shining glaze could possibly be hiding beneath that blue ink smudge, Tessa?
“泰莎，那团蓝墨水渍下面到底会藏着什么柔软又亮晶晶的糖釉呢？”欧文琢磨着到底缺了什么原料：
could possibly be hiding
could 后面加上 possibly 用来加强疑问语气，相当于“到底有可能……”。
that blue ink smudge,
smudge 指被蹭花的墨迹或污渍；遇到那一长串名词定语时，从右往左理解就对了。
Bring me that green botanical book again — our noses might read better than our eyes!
“再把那本绿皮植物书拿给我——说不定我们的鼻子比眼睛还管用呢！”泰莎忽然灵光一闪：
Bring me that green botanical book again
用 bring（带来）时，人称代词可以直接放在动词后面，不加介词；again 习惯放在句尾。
our noses might read better than our eyes!
might 表示推测，“也许、说不定”；better than 是 well 的不规则比较级。现在请按正常语速再完整听一遍这一幕。
Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!
It smells like a street festival, Owen, though the top looks surprisingly shiny.
How many spoons of coarse sugar did you sprinkle under the hot grill, Owen?
Enough to give every slice a satisfying crisp snap when your fork goes down!
Let me press my dessert fork gently right in the middle... tap, tap, clang!
Oh dear — a cake is not supposed to ring like the front desk bell, Owen!
Speaking professionally as an architect, we could roof the bicycle shed with Batch Two.
Hey! Break through the top crust and taste the warm almond cake underneath!
Oh, underneath that sugar helmet, the berries and ground almonds are delicious!
So lemon alone is too sour, and dry sugar alone turns into courtyard stone.
What soft, shining glaze could possibly be hiding beneath that blue ink smudge, Tessa?
Bring me that green botanical book again — our noses might read better than our eyes!
第二批蛋糕的糖壳结实得连屋顶冰雹都能扛住，泰莎只好再次翻开旧植物书寻找线索。回头见！
See you soon!
